steps.text: Market value break on 6758 in ESG-010: USD -1,834.02. If quantities agree, the gap is price or FX. I'll split it into a price effect and an FX effect and see which one carries it.
Same quantity (27,300). Price effect USD 0.00, FX effect USD -1,834.02, sum USD -1,834.02.
IBOR golden copy vs vendor closes
JPY/USD fixings around the as-of date
IBOR valued JPY at 0.00663415 (INTRADAY_10AM 2026-11-20); custodian used WMR 4pm 2026-11-20 at 0.00665517.
Conclusion: fx, 97% confidence. Owner: Market Data - FX.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  b.break_id,
  b.as_of,
  b.account_id,
  b.security_id,
  s.ticker,
  s.isin,
  s.currency AS sec_ccy,
  s.country,
  b.currency,
  b.break_type,
  b.ibor_value,
  b.custodian_value,
  b.difference,
  b.difference_usd,
  b.status
FROM breaks AS b
LEFT JOIN securities AS s
  ON s.security_id = b.security_id
WHERE
  b.break_id = 'BRK-0037'
LIMIT 200

SELECT
  *
FROM (
  SELECT
    'IBOR' AS book,
    quantity,
    price,
    price_date,
    fx_rate,
    fx_source,
    fx_rate_date,
    local_mv,
    base_mv
  FROM ibor_positions
  WHERE
    account_id = 'ESG-010' AND security_id = 1037
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'CUSTODIAN' AS book,
    quantity,
    price,
    as_of AS price_date,
    fx_rate,
    'WMR_4PM' AS fx_source,
    as_of AS fx_rate_date,
    local_mv,
    base_mv
  FROM custodian_positions
  WHERE
    account_id = 'ESG-010' AND security_id = 1037
) AS u
LIMIT 200

queries.sql:
SELECT
  price_date,
  source,
  close_price,
  loaded_at
FROM prices
WHERE
  security_id = 1037 AND price_date >= '2026-11-14'
ORDER BY
  price_date DESC,
  source
LIMIT 200

queries.purpose: JPY/USD fixings around the as-of date
queries.sql:
SELECT
  rate_date,
  source,
  rate_to_usd
FROM fx_rates
WHERE
  currency = 'JPY' AND rate_date >= '2026-11-16'
ORDER BY
  rate_date DESC,
  source
LIMIT 200
